queries.question: What is the longest a repair can take during the summer?

sources.snippet: 8. Repair times A repair normally takes 15 working days from the day the Repair Centre receives the product. Between May and August the Repair Centre is busier and a repair can take up to 25 working days. Customers...
sources.text:
8. Repair times
A repair normally takes 15 working days from the day the Repair Centre receives the product. Between May and August the Repair Centre is busier and a repair can take up to 25 working days. Customers should be told this when they make a claim in the summer.

9. Passing the warranty on
The warranty can be transferred once, to a second owner, if that person has the original receipt. After one transfer the warranty cannot be moved again.

sources.text:
6. Making a claim
1. The customer opens a claim on the warranty portal and enters the order number.
2. They upload at least three photographs showing the fault.
3. The Repair Centre in Sheffield assesses the claim and replies within 10 working days.
4. If the claim is accepted, the customer receives a prepaid label to send the product in.
Shop staff can start a claim on the customer's behalf at the till, using the same steps.

sources.text:
5. What is not covered
We do not cover wear and tear from ordinary use, damage from sunlight over a long time, damage from misuse, repairs or changes made by anyone else, or damage caused by washing the product incorrectly. A common example of incorrect washing is using fabric softener on a waterproof jacket, which clogs the membrane.

7. Probation and check-ins
Probation lasts 3 months. Your line manager holds three check-in meetings: one at 30 days, one at 60 days, and a final review at 90 days. Notes from each meeting are written down and you receive a copy. During probation either side can end the employment with one week of notice.

queries.question: Until what date can items bought in the Winter Sale be returned?

sources.snippet: Items bought during the Winter Sale, which runs from 1 December to 15 January, get a longer window: they can be returned until 31 January. Gifts can be returned within 60 days if the person returning them has the gift...
sources.text:
Items bought during the Winter Sale, which runs from 1 December to 15 January, get a longer window: they can be returned until 31 January.
Gifts can be returned within 60 days if the person returning them has the gift receipt. Gift returns are always refunded as store credit.

sources.snippet: 2. The return window Unused items in their original packaging can be returned within 30 days of delivery. For shop purchases the 30 days run from the date on the receipt. Clothing that has been worn outdoors counts as...
sources.text:
2. The return window
Unused items in their original packaging can be returned within 30 days of delivery. For shop purchases the 30 days run from the date on the receipt. Clothing that has been worn outdoors counts as used and cannot be returned for a change of mind.
A tent that has been pitched once on a lawn for a fit check is accepted back. A tent with peg marks, mud, or a damp smell is treated as used and is refused.

sources.snippet: 4. Items that cannot be returned The following can never be returned unless they are faulty: - Fuel canisters and any other pressurised gas product. - Embroidered or personalised items. - Underwear, socks and swimwear...
sources.text:
4. Items that cannot be returned
The following can never be returned unless they are faulty:
- Fuel canisters and any other pressurised gas product.
- Embroidered or personalised items.
- Underwear, socks and swimwear once the hygiene seal has been broken.
- Opened sleeping bag liners.
- Gift cards.

Version 4.2, effective 1 March 2026. Owner: Customer Operations.

This policy explains when a customer can return an item bought from Harbourline Outfitters, how refunds are paid, and what staff must check before they approve a return. It applies to purchases made in our shops and on the website. Faulty products are covered by the Warranty Policy, not by this one.

queries.question: On which day of the month do staff get paid?

sources.snippet: 8. Pay Salaries are paid on the last working Friday of each month. The first payment includes any days worked in the previous month. If your payslip looks wrong, tell the People Team within 5 working days so that it can...
sources.text:
8. Pay
Salaries are paid on the last working Friday of each month. The first payment includes any days worked in the previous month. If your payslip looks wrong, tell the People Team within 5 working days so that it can be fixed in the next pay run.

9. Training budget
After probation every employee can use up to 300 pounds a year on external training, such as first aid or navigation courses, with the line manager's approval.

sources.text:
Harbourline Outfitters: Leave and Time Off Policy
Version 3.4, effective 1 April 2026. Owner: People Team.

1. Annual leave
A full-time employee receives 28 days of paid annual leave per year, which includes bank holidays. Employees gain one extra day for each full year of service, up to a maximum of 33 days. Part-time staff receive the same entitlement pro rata.
The leave year runs from 1 April to 31 March.

sources.snippet: 6. Compassionate leave After the death of a spouse, partner, child or parent you receive 5 days of paid leave. For other close relatives, such as a grandparent or sibling, it is 2 days. Further unpaid time can be agreed...
sources.text:
6. Compassionate leave
After the death of a spouse, partner, child or parent you receive 5 days of paid leave. For other close relatives, such as a grandparent or sibling, it is 2 days. Further unpaid time can be agreed with your line manager.

7. Volunteering day
Every employee can take one paid day each leave year to volunteer for a registered charity. The day does not count against annual leave. Tell your line manager which charity you will help.

sources.snippet: 4. Sickness If you are ill, phone your line manager before 8:30 am on the first day. A text message or an email is not enough. You can self-certify for the first 7 calendar days of an illness. From the eighth day a fit...
sources.text:
4. Sickness
If you are ill, phone your line manager before 8:30 am on the first day. A text message or an email is not enough. You can self-certify for the first 7 calendar days of an illness. From the eighth day a fit note from a doctor is needed.
After 6 months of service you receive full pay for up to 10 days of sickness in a leave year. After those 10 days the company pays statutory sick pay only.

2. Warranty periods
The length of the warranty depends on the product:
- Tents: 3 years.
- Down jackets: 5 years.
- Waterproof shell jackets: 2 years.
- Sleeping bags: 2 years.
- Rucksacks: 5 years on seams and zips.
- Stoves: 2 years.
- Head torches: 1 year.
The period starts on the date of purchase and is shown on the receipt.

sources.text:
1. What the warranty is
Every Harbourline own-brand product comes with a warranty against manufacturing defects. The warranty does not replace the customer's statutory rights, and it is separate from the change-of-mind returns described in the Returns and Refunds Policy.
Products from other brands carry the maker's own warranty. Shop staff should direct customers to the manufacturer's claim process and must not promise a Harbourline repair for them.

sources.text:
3. Extending a sleeping bag warranty
A customer who registers a sleeping bag on the website within 28 days of buying it receives one extra year of warranty, which makes it 3 years in total. Registration is free and needs the order number.

4. What is covered
The warranty covers faults caused by how the product was made. Examples are seams that come apart, delamination of a waterproof membrane, zips that fail while being used normally, and baffles in a down jacket that split open.

sources.text:
7. Removable media
USB drives are banned unless the Security Desk has approved them and they are encrypted. Never plug in a drive you found.

8. Public Wi-Fi
When using public Wi-Fi, connect through the company VPN, which is called WireLine. Shop and office guest Wi-Fi is on a separate network and has no route to internal systems.

9. Backups
Company systems are backed up every night. Backups are kept for 35 days. The restore process is tested once every quarter.

9. Company cards
Company cards have a limit of 1,000 pounds. If a card is lost or stolen, tell Finance straight away and report it to the bank within 24 hours. Card statements must be matched to receipts by the 5th of the following month.

10. Home working equipment
Employees who work from home can claim a one-off allowance of 250 pounds for a chair, desk or monitor. Keep the receipt. The equipment belongs to the company and must be returned when you leave.

3. How we talk to customers
Use the customer's name. Apologise once, sincerely, and then move on to fixing the problem. Never tell a customer to calm down. Do not blame the carrier, the warehouse or another team in front of the customer. If you do not know the answer, say so and promise a time when you will come back with it.

Do not store a sleeping bag compressed for longer than 2 weeks. At home, keep it loose in a large mesh sack. Wash a sleeping bag no more than once a year, because each wash reduces the loft. A liner is the best way to keep a bag clean.
